body.purpose: The promise line and the quiet aside.

value.purpose: Live values on the range controls, in tabular numerals.

aside.purpose: The quiet placard paragraph on desktop and the mobile lede.

hint.purpose: The one instruction line under the field; pointer-aware.

display-mobile.purpose: The name on phones and portrait tablets.

display-compact.purpose: The name on short phone screens.

display-mid.purpose: The name on short desktop windows.

shadows.name: field-recess
shadows.purpose: The eyepiece wall; the only inner depth in the page.

shadows.name: page-lift
shadows.purpose: Separates the circular field from the dark page without a glow.

shadows.name: thumb-seat
shadows.purpose: Keeps the brass range thumb grounded on its track.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Interface arrives once, after the star's first frame.

motion.name: state

motion.name: body-pulse
motion.purpose: The living star breathes; reduced-motion holds it still.

components.name: Eyepiece Field
components.description: The circular field that holds the star, with a knurled brass bezel and a deep inner recess.
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; width: min(70dvh, 48vw, 46rem); aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 47%, #151009 0%, #0a0809 52%, #060608 100%); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(193,154,105,0.28), 0 0 0 7px rgba(193,154,105,0.045), inset 0 0 74px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.94), inset 0 0 16px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.8), 0 2rem 5rem -3rem rgba(0,0,0,0.9); } .ds-field-glow { position: absolute; inset: 24%; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, #ffe3c6 0%, rgba(255,196,140,0.5) 38%, rgba(255,140,80,0) 72%); } .ds-field-scale { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -0.25deg, rgba(205,166,116,0.42) 0deg 0.5deg, transparent 0.5deg 6deg); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(circle closest-side, transparent calc(100% - 12px), #000 calc(100% - 12px) calc(100% - 8px), transparent calc(100% - 8px)); mask: radial-gradient(circle closest-side, transparent calc(100% - 12px), #000 calc(100% - 12px) calc(100% - 8px), transparent calc(100% - 8px)); }

components.name: Instrument Readout
components.description: Three live measurements in tabular numerals, divided from the header by a hairline.
components.css: .ds-readout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 16px; width: 100%; max-width: 27rem; padding: 15px 0 18px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(193,154,105,0.24); } .ds-readout span { display: block; margin-bottom: 6px; font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11.2px; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8c7f6c; } .ds-readout b { font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.1px; font-weight: 400; color: #efe4d2; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Range Control
components.description: A fine brass rail with a knurled brass thumb and a tabular value at the right.
components.css: .ds-control { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 5.6rem 1fr 3.6rem; align-items: center; gap: 13.6px; padding: 7.2px 0 2.4px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(193,154,105,0.24); font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-control > span { font-size: 11.2px; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #b3a591; } .ds-control output { font-size: 12.5px; text-align: right; color: #efe4d2; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-control input { -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none; width: 100%; height: 36px; margin: 0; background: transparent; cursor: ew-resize; } .ds-control input::-webkit-slider-runnable-track { height: 1px; background: linear-gradient(to right, #c19a69 0 68%, rgba(193,154,105,0.22) 68% 100%); } .ds-control input::-webkit-slider-thumb { -webkit-appearance: none; width: 16px; height: 16px; margin-top: -8px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid rgba(255,226,188,0.32); background: repeating-conic-gradient(rgba(23,16,9,0.5) 0deg 9deg, rgba(255,220,170,0.4) 9deg 18deg), radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #f1d5a8, #966c36 72%); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.85), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.45); } .ds-control input:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid rgba(255,207,148,0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Release Button
components.description: The one verb. It names the next action on the left and the body's state on the right.
components.css: .ds-release { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; width: 100%; max-width: 27rem; min-height: 53.6px; margin-top: 10.4px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(193,154,105,0.24); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #efe4d2; font-family: 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 300ms, background-color 300ms, color 300ms; } .ds-release span:first-child { font-size: 11.2px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-release span:last-child { font-size: 11.2px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #8c7f6c; } .ds-release:hover { border-color: rgba(193,154,105,0.5); background: rgba(193,154,105,0.05); } .ds-release:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #ffcf94; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-release[aria-pressed="true"] { color: #ff8a45; border-color: rgba(255,138,69,0.38); } .ds-release[aria-pressed="true"] span:last-child { color: rgba(255,138,69,0.72); }

narrative.overview:
The page is one turn at a public observatory. The star is not a poster; it is what sits in the eyepiece when the instrument is pointed and the visitor finally holds still. Everything around it belongs to the instrument: a knurled brass bezel, a measured scale, a placard set in two voices, and three controls that a hand would find in the dark.

The scene is a dark room at night, so the ground is near-black rather than slate. The only strong light is the body itself, a champagne-and-gold particle volume with a cream core and an ember edge. Interface ink is warm ivory, never pure white; brass is the metal, amber is attention, and ember appears only when the body is released. Depth comes from one recessed circular field and hairline rules, not from cards, glass, or elevation.

The piece is quiet at rest and authored in motion: the body assembles once, breathes, drifts, notices the cursor, and can be let go and called back. Nothing on the page claims a real observation.
keyCharacteristics: A single circular field is the hero; the UI is its collar.
Champagne light against near-black ink, with brass as the only metal.
Bodoni Moda display, Archivo instrument voice, tabular numerals.
Square controls, hairline rules, one circular exception.
One authored reform moment; the rest is slow drift.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: The brightest element is always the star. Interface text never exceeds the luminance of the body's midtone, and no chrome gets a glow.

rules.name: The Ember Exception Rule
rules.body: Ember is spent only on the released state. If it appears anywhere else, the state language collapses.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Bodoni never sets a control label and Archivo never sets the title. The only crossing is the italic display word, which is a name, not a label.

rules.name: The No Glow Chrome Rule
rules.body: Emissive bloom belongs to the particles. Chrome gets hairlines and neutral shadows only; a colored halo on a control is a bug.

rules.name: The One Circle Rule
rules.body: A second circle anywhere in the chrome competes with the eyepiece. Do not round buttons, inputs, or panels.

rules.name: The Named State Rule
rules.body: The button always names the next action (Release / Recollect) and the right side always names the current body (assembled / dispersed). No icon, no ellipsis, no spinner.

dos: Do keep the star the brightest thing; interface luminance stays below its midtone.
Do use tabular numerals for every live value.
Do keep functional text at 0.7rem (11.2px) or larger.
Do keep the field's bezel scale and the instrument's readout honest to real state.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: no intro assembly, no auto-orbit, a quarter of the twinkle.
donts: Don't put the controls in a card, a glass panel, or a rounded container.
Don't add a colored glow to a control, a border, or text.
Don't use ember outside the released state.
Don't use a second circular container or pill; the eyepiece is the only circle.
Don't claim a real object, coordinates, or data; the note says the field is composed.
